question: How many credits does one second of AI video cost the customer?
why_it_matters: fal.ai charges the company $0.0562 per second of video (about $1.69 for 30 seconds) plus the voice. The rate must cover that, Razorpay's fee, tax and your margin, at a dollar-to-rupee rate you choose.
default_if_unanswered: None. The rate is built as a setting with no value; M3 cannot finish without it.

question: How should customers log in: email and password, Google sign-in, phone OTP, or a mix?
why_it_matters: It decides what is built in M2 and which outside services are needed (email sender, SMS sender, Google project).
default_if_unanswered: Email and password with email verification (decision D-003). Not started without your answer.
answer: Email and password (owner, 2026-11-17). Decision D-003 confirmed.

question: Is GST charged on top of the credit amount, included in it, or not applicable? Are tax invoices required?
why_it_matters: It changes what the customer pays for 100 credits and what records each payment must keep. This needs your accountant; engineering cannot decide it.
default_if_unanswered: Build charges exactly ₹N for N credits with no tax line. Launch waits for the answer.

question: Which service sends verification and password-reset emails, and from which address?
why_it_matters: Needed for real sign-ups. Development prints emails to the console, so this does not block building.
default_if_unanswered: Console output in development; choose a provider before launch.

question: What is the refund policy, and do credits expire?
why_it_matters: Decides how refunds are handled in M6 and what the terms say.
default_if_unanswered: Credits do not expire and cannot be cashed out. Failed videos return credits automatically. Payment refunds are done by an admin in Razorpay and reverse the credits.

question: Can customers buy any amount, or only fixed packs? What are the smallest and largest purchases?
why_it_matters: Shapes the buy-credits screen and the server-side limits.
default_if_unanswered: Any whole-rupee amount from ₹50 to ₹10,000 per purchase. These two limits are engineering placeholders, not researched figures.

question: Where will the platform be hosted (cloud provider and region)?
why_it_matters: Decides where customers' photos and payment records are kept, and the deployment work in M7.
default_if_unanswered: Develop locally; nothing is deployed until you choose.

question: Is listening to the generated voice free with a daily limit, or should each voice generation cost credits?
why_it_matters: Each voice generation costs the company money even if the customer never makes the video.
default_if_unanswered: Free, only when the wallet covers the estimated video price, capped at 20 voice generations per user per day. The cap of 20 is an engineering placeholder.

question: How long are customers' photos, audio and videos kept?
why_it_matters: Photos of people are personal data; storage also costs money.
default_if_unanswered: Keep until the customer deletes them. Launch waits for a retention period.

question: Is there a Razorpay account, and can you provide test-mode keys and a webhook secret?
why_it_matters: Payment code can be written and mock-tested without them, but cannot be proven against Razorpay.
default_if_unanswered: M4 stops at MOCK-VERIFIED.

question: What exact wording must a customer agree to before using a person's photo, and who are the first admins?
why_it_matters: The consent text is stored with every video; admins can change balances.
default_if_unanswered: A plain statement that the customer is the person shown or has their permission. Admins are set by a command, not in the interface.

question: Has a lawyer confirmed whether a prepaid credit wallet used only on this platform needs any regulatory registration in India?
why_it_matters: Not verified by engineering. It could change whether credits may be refunded or transferred.
default_if_unanswered: Credits stay non-transferable and cannot be cashed out. Launch waits for the answer.

question: Do you approve a paid live run of the full voice-and-video flow on fal.ai before launch?
why_it_matters: The README says the fal.ai integration has not been run live end to end. No paid call is made without your approval.
default_if_unanswered: No live run; everything stays MOCK-VERIFIED.

question: Who supplies the first banner clips, and in what size and format?
why_it_matters: The template picker needs real clips to show. Clips are converted to match each AI video, so any common MP4 works.
default_if_unanswered: You provide MP4 clips of 2 to 3 seconds; the build uses plain placeholder clips until then.

question: Must every video have banners, or are they optional?
why_it_matters: Decides whether the picker offers 'None' and whether the company's branding appears on every video.
default_if_unanswered: Optional: none, start only, end only, or both.

question: Should a banner clip's own sound play, or are banners silent?
why_it_matters: Decides how clips are prepared and whether the video starts with music or silence.
default_if_unanswered: The clip's sound plays if it has any; otherwise that part is silent.

question: If joining the banners fails even after retries, should the customer get the AI video without banners and be charged, or get nothing and be refunded?
why_it_matters: By then the company has already paid fal.ai for the AI video. Refunding means the company bears that cost; charging means the customer pays for a video without the banners they chose.
default_if_unanswered: Deliver the AI video without banners, charge as normal, tell the customer, and flag the job for staff.

question: What makes a talking-avatar video good enough to sell: how realistic must it be, at what resolution, and is quality or low cost more important?
why_it_matters: There are no acceptance criteria for output quality yet. They decide whether the current 'standard' model tier is enough and how the live run in M7 is judged.
default_if_unanswered: Keep the current standard-tier model; judge quality with you at the first approved live run.

question: When a paid request to fal.ai is cut off and we cannot tell whether fal.ai accepted it, who bears the cost?
why_it_matters: The request is never retried, to avoid paying twice. The customer got no video, but the company may still have been billed.
default_if_unanswered: The customer's credits are returned; the company bears any fal.ai charge; the job is flagged for staff (decision D-005).

question: Do you approve the screen designs and the proposed colours and typefaces on the design canvas?
why_it_matters: No screen is rebuilt until you approve. The palette and typefaces are engineering's proposal, not a brand you chose.
default_if_unanswered: None. The component library and every later screen wait for your approval.
answer: Approved (owner, 2026-11-17), after the login and sign-up screens were given an illustrated brand panel at the owner's request.

question: What is the product's name?
why_it_matters: It appears in the wordmark, the browser tab, emails and the Razorpay checkout window.
default_if_unanswered: The working name 'Talking Avatar'. Changing it later is a small edit.
answer: Frameforge. Backend: Frameforge API. Frontend: Frameforge Web (owner, 2026-11-17; decision D-031).

question: Should customers be able to reset a forgotten password by email?
why_it_matters: The login design has a 'Forgot password?' link but no reset screen or flow is planned. Without one, a locked-out paying customer needs manual help. It also requires the system to send email.
default_if_unanswered: Yes: add a reset screen and an emailed link to M2.
answer: Yes: implement the forgot-password flow (owner, 2026-11-17). Designed now; built in M2 (T-203, T-210) because it needs customer accounts. HLD section 5.5.
